title: Choose the research dashboard structure
question: Which structure best communicates the Topic 2 findings to a supervisor or thesis jury?

options.label: Research Evidence Map
options.lineage: evidence maps and scientific argument graphs
options.thesis: The three research questions form one connected map from claim to evidence and limitation.
options.viewport: A central Topic 2 thesis connects three RQ panels, each showing its verdict, evidence strength, and primary result.
options.risk: The spatial model may be slower to scan during a linear jury presentation.

options.label: Jury Briefing
options.lineage: scientific briefing decks and executive research summaries
options.thesis: A guided narrative turns the study into a concise three-act defense of the findings.
options.viewport: An executive verdict leads into RQ chapters with one key figure, one interpretation, and one limitation each.
options.risk: The presentation flow offers less freedom for exploratory model and dataset comparison.

options.label: RQ Evidence Spine
options.lineage: reproducible research reports and evidence synthesis
options.thesis: A single vertical spine gives every research question the same rigorous claim-to-evidence anatomy.
options.viewport: A sticky RQ rail accompanies a verdict, key comparison, confidence note, source, and limitation for each question.
options.risk: The complete report becomes long and needs strong navigation on smaller screens.
